questions.question: A company is designing a web application that must be highly available across multiple AWS regions. The application uses a MySQL database that needs to be replicated with minimal latency. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment in a single region
Use Amazon Aurora Global Database with read replicas in multiple regions
Use Amazon DynamoDB with global tables
Use Amazon RDS with manual snapshots copied to other regions

questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora Global Database is designed for globally distributed applications, allowing a single Aurora database to span multiple AWS regions. It provides fast replication with typical latency of less than 1 second, and enables low-latency global reads. Multi-AZ is only within a single region (A is incorrect). DynamoDB Global Tables would work but the question specifically mentions MySQL (C is incorrect). Manual snapshots don't provide real-time replication (D is incorrect). Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html
questions.notes: This question tests understanding of multi-region database replication options
